values.message_text: Server latency spiked to 900ms during the release window; we lost about 12% of requests.

seed_edits.reason: Design requires Robert Walsh to have authored a message reporting a concrete numeric problem in #engineering this week; no such message existed in the base seed (his existing engineering message about login rate limiting lacks the specified concrete-number framing), so it must be added to instantiate the robert_walsh alternative role faithfully.

Design's robert_silent_member negative role requires a third user named Robert who is a documented channel member of #core-infra but has authored no messages, contrasting membership from authorship; this user does not exist in the base seed and must be added.
New user Robert Kim needs workspace membership to be a coherent, discoverable seed record consistent with other channel members.
Design specifies Robert Kim holds a channel_members row for #core-infra alongside the other listed members, establishing the membership-without-authorship contrast for the negative role.

notes: Obligation 1 is genuinely underspecified: both Robert Walsh (U03ROBERT23, via his new #engineering message about 900ms latency/12% request loss) and Robert Chen (U_ROBERT, via his existing #core-infra message about the $47K budget overage) satisfy 'named Robert + numeric-problem message + bounded technical channel corpus,' so the selector's union covers both and the solver must recognize the ambiguity rather than silently pick one. Robert Kim (U_ROBERTK) is a negative: added purely as a #core-infra channel_members row with no authored messages, testing that membership alone does not satisfy the MESSAGE-authorship leg of the route. Kenji Sato (U_KENJI) is a negative: he reports numbers in #product-growth, which lies outside the bounded corpus (engineering/core-infra) and he is not named Robert. Robert Walsh's #general message (1700173200.000456) is a same-author negative: non-numeric content and out-of-corpus channel, so it does not add or resolve anything beyond his real qualifying #engineering message. Obligation 2 (the follow-up DM) cannot be bound to a single existing referent because the request cannot be uniquely resolved between the two Roberts before conversations.open/chat.postMessage; its selector instead defines the generic acceptance shape (a message in a DM channel whose membership includes a user named Robert) for whichever channel the solver legitimately opens, consistent with the design's stated resolution mode. The acting user (U01AGENBOT9) already holds channel_members rows in both #engineering (C03IJKL9012) and #core-infra (C_INFRA), giving documented API access to both bounded channels' histories via conversations.history without relying on hidden seed knowledge.
